heroDescription: A sourced guide to the franchise timeline, championship eras, defining players, iconic numbers and the fan culture that shaped Seattle football.
timelineKicker: From expansion team to two-time champion

timeline.title: Seattle is awarded an NFL franchise
timeline.description: The NFL granted Seattle its expansion franchise on June 4, setting the stage for the club to begin play in 1976.

timeline.title: Football arrives at the Kingdome
timeline.description: The expansion Seahawks played their first season in the NFC, with Jim Zorn and Steve Largent beginning a partnership that helped define the early club.

timeline.title: The first playoff run
timeline.description: In Chuck Knox’s first season, Seattle beat Denver and Miami before its breakthrough postseason ended in the AFC Championship Game.

timeline.title: No. 12 is retired for the fans
timeline.description: Seattle retired the number 12 on December 15 as a tribute to the home crowd and its impact on games.

timeline.title: A Kingdome roar changes the rules
timeline.description: The NFL briefly introduced an excessive-crowd-noise rule during an era when visiting offenses struggled to communicate inside the Kingdome.

timeline.title: The franchise stays in the Northwest
timeline.description: Paul Allen’s purchase secured the Seahawks’ future in the Pacific Northwest and cleared the way for a new stadium project.

timeline.title: A new outdoor home
timeline.description: The Seahawks opened their new stadium, beginning the venue era that continues today at Lumen Field.

timeline.title: Seattle returns to the NFC
timeline.description: NFL realignment moved the Seahawks from the AFC West to the NFC West, the conference where they had played their inaugural season.

timeline.title: The 12 Flag tradition begins
timeline.description: Twelve original season-ticket holders raised the 12 Flag before the October 12 home game, launching a lasting pregame ritual.

timeline.title: The first NFC crown
timeline.description: A 13–3 team powered by Shaun Alexander, Matt Hasselbeck and Walter Jones won the NFC and reached the franchise’s first Super Bowl.

timeline.title: Beast Quake shakes Seattle
timeline.description: Marshawn Lynch’s 67-yard playoff touchdown against New Orleans sent the stadium crowd into a celebration measured by a nearby seismic station.

timeline.title: Defense carries Seattle to the summit
timeline.description: The top-seeded Seahawks capped a dominant season by winning Super Bowl XLVIII, the first league championship in franchise history.

timeline.title: Back-to-back NFC champions
timeline.description: Seattle returned to the Super Bowl after winning a second consecutive NFC championship.

timeline.title: A second Lombardi Trophy
timeline.description: A 14–3 regular season ended with Seattle defeating New England 29–13 in Super Bowl LX for the franchise’s second league championship.

eras.title: Kingdome beginnings
eras.description: Jim Zorn’s improvisation and Steve Largent’s precision gave the expansion club its first personality. Chuck Knox’s hard-running teams then delivered Seattle’s first deep playoff run.

eras.title: Holmgren’s offense
eras.description: Matt Hasselbeck, Shaun Alexander and a line anchored by Walter Jones powered the 2005 team to 13 wins and the franchise’s first NFC championship.

eras.title: Legion of Boom
eras.description: The 2013 defense led the NFL in points allowed, yards allowed and takeaways, then overwhelmed Denver in Super Bowl XLVIII.

eras.title: A new champion
eras.description: The 2025 Seahawks paired a 14–3 regular season with a defense that held New England scoreless for three quarters in Super Bowl LX.

methodology: Timeline claims are paraphrased from the linked source on each entry. We prioritize the Pro Football Hall of Fame, HistoryLink’s Washington history encyclopedia, Lumen Field, and team-published records. Numbers are included only when those sources state them directly. This page favors defining moments over completeness.
